layers.process: Under the Laccadive, Minicoy and Amindivi Islands (Restriction on Entry and Residence) Rules 1967, everyone who isn't a native of the islands needs a permit to enter and stay, apart from government officials and armed forces members on duty and their families. Foreign tourists also need a valid passport and Indian visa. Apply on the e-Permit portal; from 15 October 2026 applications move to the new portal at lak.e-permit.utl.gov.in. Tourist applications no longer need a local sponsor or a police clearance certificate, and one form covers up to six people.

zone-requirements.note: Lakshadweep isn't in the Protected or Restricted Area schedules of the 2025 Order; its own permit applies. Travel guides (signal, not read on an official page) say foreigners may visit only Agatti, Bangaram and Kadmat; check the islands the permit form offers.

laws.rule: Everyone, Indians included, needs an entry permit from the Lakshadweep Administration, issued through the e-permit portal under the Entry Permit Rules.

Alcohol was long banned except on Bangaram. A new Lakshadweep Excise Regulation was gazetted in August 2026 to allow alcohol under licences and permits; ask your permit authority or resort what applies.
